Evaluate the following economic assertions:

title: Cash and Cash Equivalents
statements: Classifying a laptop computer as a non-current asset depends on management's intention to use it in operations rather than to sell it quickly.
When a laptop computer is acquired to be resold rather than used, it belongs among current assets as inventory.
Classifying a packaging line as a non-current asset depends mainly on its purchase price rather than on management's intended use.
A laptop computer bought by a business to support its own daily operations is a tangible fixed asset because it delivers benefit across several accounting periods.
A packaging line acquired for resale still counts among non-current assets as long as it remains unsold for several months.
